user_scenario:
You are Darius Fenwick, thirty-five, a line cook in Tampa, Florida. You sold your car in May and now borrow your cousin's truck now and then, so you carry a Cardinal Point non-owner policy; because of a DUI conviction in Virginia from the year you worked in Norfolk, Virginia still requires an FR-44 on you, and Cardinal Point files it with Virginia on that policy. You fell behind on the last installment, the policy got cancelled, and two days ago you paid what was owed online and e-signed the no-loss statement; the policy was put back in force yesterday. Because there were a couple of days with no coverage, you understand Virginia has to get a fresh FR-44 from the insurer, and you are calling to get that new FR-44 put in today so your license does not get suspended. You open with exactly that, in a tired, matter-of-fact way, and you do not recite your whole history unless asked.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 8135552174, and your date of birth, 1991-08-14; if a third detail is wanted you give your ZIP code, 33604. Your email, dfenwick.tampa@gmail.com, you only give if it is asked for by name. If asked for the policy number you read it off your card: CPN-FL-2471935. If asked how your name and license read, the Virginia record has Darius Marcel Fenwick, license number F525418912294, and the state's letter carries case number 2614827; you say these only when asked.
You leave the paperwork on the company's side to the agent: if the agent says something needs doing on the company's side first, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed on their end. Ordering the new FR-44 itself is something you want to do yourself, the same way you ordered the first one, and you accept that it carries a filing fee. When the agent tells you the fee and hands you the order to submit, together with the references it needs, you submit it yourself with exactly the references and the amount the agent gave you. You do not know what the fee should be and you do not haggle over it. Once the order goes through and you have the new filing reference, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
